title: Load Testing & Bottleneck Analysis: Percentiles, Load Profiles, Saturation & Valid Benchmarks
concept: Find the first bottleneck with numbers you can defend: latency, throughput and concurrency, percentiles instead of averages, load profiles, coordinated omission, warm-up, the saturation knee, Little's Law, comparisons that beat the noise, and turning load tests into SLOs and capacity plans.
description: An expert course for engineers who are asked "will it hold on exam day?". Every lesson starts from an incident on the CodeDev learning platform - a report that said the average was 120 ms while learners waited 6 seconds, a load generator that hid its own stalls, a benchmark that compared a cold run with a warm one, a submit endpoint that fell over at 340 requests per second while CPU sat at 40% - and answers it with analysis you can check: latency versus throughput, percentiles from samples, load profiles, throughput and error rates, coordinated omission, warm-up, the Find the First Bottleneck scenario, the saturation knee, significant differences, Little's Law, benchmark validity, SLOs, chaos experiments and capacity plans. 15 lessons with True/False quizzes on real load test output and dashboards, and Python challenges graded by hidden tests on recorded results.

learningOutcomes.text: Report latency with percentiles from raw samples instead of averages
Design load profiles and compute throughput and error rates from load test results
Keep measurements valid: coordinated omission, warm-up and differences larger than the noise
Find the saturation knee and the first bottleneck, and reason with Little's Law
Turn load test results into SLOs, chaos experiments and a capacity plan
